_comment: Single source of truth for constants that exist on both the JS and PHP sides. Imported via JSON in src/components/constants.js (webpack handles JSON natively) and read via motion_blocks_shared_constants() in animation-plugin.php. Adding a new shared constant: add it here, then expose it through both consumer paths.
_README_schemaDefaults: 'schemaDefaults' is the SCHEMA default of each animation attribute: the value an attribute has when it is missing from a block's saved comment. WordPress omits any attribute equal to its schema default when it saves a block, and refills it from the schema when the editor loads the block. So this map defines what every omitted key means, on both sides:
- JS: addAnimationAttributes in src/index.js registers each attribute with `default: SCHEMA_DEFAULTS.<key>`.

- PHP: motion_blocks_render_block merges this map under the saved attributes before reading them, so the front end resolves omitted keys exactly as the editor does. motion_blocks_attr_default() reads the same map.

Changing a value here changes the effective setting of every existing block that relied on the old default, in the editor and on the front end alike. Treat the values as frozen unless that is the intent.

What a NEW block gets when the user picks a mode lives in DEFAULT_ATTRIBUTES in src/components/constants.js (JS only). It starts from this map and overrides a few keys: animationDelay and animationEntryDelay are 0 for new blocks but 0.4 here, because blocks saved before that preference changed rely on 0.4. The mode picker writes the preference explicitly, and since it differs from the schema default it is serialized into the block comment.
Not listed: attributes whose schema default is null (Custom From/To values) and editor-only UI state. A missing key already means 'not set' to PHP.
